summary: This study compares two fabricated Ti3C2Tx electrode architectures: a multilayer exfoliated powder-based electrode and a binder- and additive-free Ti3C2Tx paper made by delaminating and filtering few-layer flakes. Both derive from HF-etched Ti3AlC2 and were tested across several aqueous cation-containing electrolytes; these electrolyte tests are measurement conditions rather than separately fabricated electrodes. The Ti3C2Tx paper is the headline electrode and achieved up to 350 F/cm3 in KOH, while also showing almost no degradation after 10,000 galvanostatic cycles at 1 A/g. Exact mass loading, thickness, pore metrics, and a text-stated exact maximum gravimetric capacitance are not provided in the supplied article text.
